messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need a tiny config proposal for geo-aware routing + tiered fallback + quota enforcement. Goal: predictable behavior when Europe capacity is constrained and free/pro customers hit soft quotas.
kevin: high level: check quota -> pick regional pool -> choose model variant -> apply fallback. but order matters for billing/telemetry.
dina: +1 but we also need a grace policy for short spikes. free should degrade to smaller model quickly, enterprise should spill to other region or reserved capacity.
maria: idea: split enforcement into 'pre-routing' and 'post-routing' checks. pre-routing rejects hard quota breaches immediately; post-routing logs and triggers adaptive fallback when latency or capacity issues show up.
sam (SRE): watch out: pre-routing reject causes poor UX. for free tier maybe we should prefer soft-deny (throttle) vs hard 403.
kevin: can we express this in a compact spec? draft config snippet: ```yaml
routing_policies:
  - name: geo-tiered-default
    tiers: [free, pro, enterprise]
    order: [quota_check, region_select, variant_select, fallback]
    quota:
      free: {soft_limit: 10000, hard_limit: 12000, soft_behavior: throttle}
      pro:  {soft_limit: 200000, hard_limit: 250000, soft_behavior: degrade}
      enterprise: {soft_limit: 0, hard_limit: 0}
    region_preferences:
      eu: {preferred: true, fallback_regions: [us-east, us-west]}
    fallback_chain:
      - smaller_quant
      - older_checkpoint
      - cross_region
```
dina: nice. couple notes: 1) enterprise should have cross_region=true always. 2) soft_behavior for pro should prefer variant downgrade before throttling.
maria: telemetry requirement: tag every decision with fields: tier, quota_state (ok|soft|hard), selected_variant, fallback_step, served_region — we need these in Console dashboard.
kevin: agree. and we should increment a metric 'routing.fallback.count' with labels (tier, region_from, region_to, step).
sam (SRE): ops concern: cross_region spikes can create inter-region charges. need opt-in per tenant or a max-cross-region spend cap. suggest: per-tenant 'cross_region_budget' with an automatic cutoff.
dina: UX on Console: show allowed cross-region budget and current burn rate + toggle. for free tenants it should be off by default.
maria: question for API: should the routing decision be visible in the response headers? e.g., `X-Redwood-Routing: eu->us-east;variant=quant8;quota=soft`
kevin: i'd prefer a minimal header that includes final_variant and quota_state. full decision dump can be pulled from `GET /internal/routing/{request_id}` for privacy.
ai-router-bot: Canary check: eu pool at 83% capacity, quant8 nodes healthy, cross_region bandwidth 12Gbps available.
sam (SRE): ops note: add a circuit-breaker that prevents >10% of traffic from a single tenant going cross-region for more than 5m. prevents noisy neighbor tears.
dina: edge case: what happens if pre-routing sees quota ok but region selects a variant that would exceed variant-specific capacity? should fallback be recursive?
kevin: yes recursive fallback: variant -> smaller variant -> cross-region -> reject. each step increments `routing.attempts`. put a max_attempts=4 default.
maria: I'll sketch the final PR description: short summary, the YAML spec above, telemetry fields, Console wireframe notes (budget toggle, fallback timeline), and SRE guardrails (cross-region cap + circuit-breaker).
kevin: can you add a sample response header and an example `GET /internal/routing` payload? small one for docs.
maria: will do. action items: @dina wireframe for console, @sam add circuit-breaker tests, @kevin API header + internal endpoint example, i'll author the PR.
dina: on it :+1:
sam (SRE): will add chaos scenarios to the test matrix.
maria: thanks all. we should aim for PR by end of week.
